LSPV-5/REFEREE391 (2026-11-06 10:48 PST) forces a Resolution chain before AND3 in every remaining 35-node bridge proof.

**PROVED/RESTRICTED + COMPUTATIONAL:** complete historical source-once closure gives 183 AND3-admissible conditions and 3,234 clauses per authenticated 18-source side. None of the 33,489 cross-side condition pairs has combined support at most three. Every nonempty side-local internal-row XOR sum has support at least two, so a mixed XOR lineage has support at least four and cannot feed historical AND3. Therefore the lowest cross-cut ancestor of REFEREE390's required cross-cut affine block must be strict Resolution.

Exact enumeration of all 4,056,196 legal cross-side strict Resolution pairs finds 4,056,196 distinct resolvents, minimum support four, and zero support-at-most-three outputs. Thus the first cross resolvent cannot feed AND3 directly: at least one further strict Resolution is compulsory before the required cross-cut AND3.

A separate base-3 implementation reconstructed the source and reproduced every condition, clause, pair and support count; it rejected nine hostile mutations. A symbolic row checker rejected five more. Primary enumeration used 37.450 s / 422,992 KiB; independent verification 56.023 s / 507,280 KiB. No authoritative historical accepted-byte checker was run.

The interval remains $35\le W_{R_{\rm mix341}}(F_{\rm bridge})\le37$. The source-disjoint continuation after the first cross resolvent, all 36-node classes, full historical all-rule superpolynomial growth, B1/B2/B3 and P versus NP remain OPEN.
